title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a field of characteristic ≠ 2. E/k is an elliptic curve presented through the degree-2 quotient map p : E → E/{±1} ≅ P^1_k. This map is branched over the three roots z_i of Z^3 + a_1 Z^2 + a_2 Z + a_3 and over ∞, and the origin 0_E lies over ∞. From the previous page, the set J = ₂E* of non-zero 2-torsion points corresponds to the divisor D_J ⊂ Σ_J ≅ P^1_k.

First paragraph: a point x ≠ 0 of E(k) is the same as two pieces of data.
- Its image x_0 = p(x) ∈ k.
- A choice of one of the two square roots X' of x_0^3 + a_1 x_0^2 + a_2 x_0 + a_3. The two roots are distinct iff the right-hand side is ≠ 0, i.e. iff x_0 ∉ D_J, i.e. iff x ∉ ₂E*.
- The chosen root is X' = p'(x).
So (p, p') are affine Weierstrass coordinates for E in the form y^2 = cubic in x. This is the usual ℘, ℘' picture written algebraically, with p defined intrinsically as the quotient by the involution.

Proposition 3: for x, y, z ∈ E(k) \ {0}, pairwise distinct, x + y + z = 0 iff det[[1, p(x), p'(x)], [1, p(y), p'(y)], [1, p(z), p'(z)]] = 0. This is collinearity of the three points in the Weierstrass plane model.

Right-margin remark: under (41) with distinct points, p(x), p(y), p(z) are pairwise distinct. If p(x) = p(y) then either x = y, which is excluded, or x = −y, which forces z = 0, a contradiction.

Left-margin NB: if x, y, z are not all distinct, (42) holds trivially (two equal rows) but does not imply x + y + z = 0. A second, partly illegible note concerns the degenerate case x = y = z = a, where the condition becomes 3a = 0 with a ≠ 0 (flex points).

Proof (started here, finished on p.110):
- By the definition of the group law via divisor classes, x + y + z = 0 iff {x} + {y} + {z} ~ 3{0}.
- For nonzero points this means there is a rational function f in F_3 = L(3·0), with a pole of order exactly 3 at 0 and no other pole, whose zero divisor is {x} + {y} + {z}.
- Up to a scalar, f = p' + αp + β. So the column vector (p'(x), p'(y), p'(z)) is a linear combination of (p(x), p(y), p(z)) and (1, 1, 1), which gives the determinant condition.
- Conversely, distinctness makes (1, 1, 1) and (p(·)) independent, so f exists, and its divisor is forced.

Purpose: the page sets up explicit coordinates and the explicit group law. These are needed for Grothendieck's description of the moduli of elliptic curves with level structure (here the structure J = ₂E*) in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: No mathematical error. The proposition and the margin argument are correct, and the margin NB correctly identifies why the distinctness hypothesis is needed.

Minor: the statement only treats pairwise distinct points. Tangent and flex cases are relegated to marginal notes and not stated as a full criterion; for those one would need multiplicities or the derivative of the determinant.

ideas.what: Description of points of E as (p(x), choice of square root of the cubic), where p : E → E/±1 ≅ P^1 is the quotient map and p' is the second coordinate.
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass model y^2 = f(x) (char ≠ 2) via the hyperelliptic/Kummer quotient E → P^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (analytic ℘, ℘'); algebraic version classical, e.g. Silverman, Deuring

ideas.what: x + y + z = 0 iff the three points are collinear, expressed as the vanishing of the 3×3 determinant in (1, p, p'); proved via L(3·0) = <1, p, p'> and linear equivalence {x} + {y} + {z} ~ 3{0}.
ideas.modern_name: Chord-and-tangent group law / collinearity criterion via Riemann–Roch
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Newton/Poincaré chord construction; Riemann–Roch proof standard in Silverman, Hartshorne)

deep.surprise_reason: This is entirely textbook material: the Weierstrass coordinates and the determinant form of the collinearity law. Its only interest is as evidence of the explicit, coordinate-level groundwork Grothendieck laid for his elliptic-curve moduli notes.
transcription_corrections: '(distinctes moins si la 2e est ≠ 0' should read approximately '(distinctes ssi le 2e membre est ≠ 0, i.e. si x_0 ∉ J = ₂E*, i.e. x_0 ∉ D_J ⊂ Σ_J)'.
The handwritten function is Grothendieck's 'p' and 'p'' (p(x), p'(x)), not a printed ℘. In (40) it is X' = p'(x).
Left-margin NB reads approximately: 'NB Si deux de x, y, z sont égaux, (41) implique (42) (trivial), mais (42) n'implique pas x + y + z = 0 !'
The 'Proposition 3' hypothesis reads: 'Soient x, y, z ∈ E(k) \ {0}, tous distincts, alors on a ...'.
Lower-left margin, approximately: 'La condition (41) (avec x, y, z non tous distincts) équivaut à : ∃ a ∈ E(k) ... x = y = z = a ... avec a + a + a = 0 et a ≠ 0'. Partly conjectural.
